intro: A query embedding and document embeddings share a coordinate space. Retrieval ranks document vectors by their similarity to the query.
task: Return a Python list of row indices for the k largest cosine similarities, descending. Break equal scores by ascending row index.
requirements: query is a nonempty 1D vector; vectors is a nonempty 2D matrix with the same feature count.
k is an integer between 0 and the number of rows, inclusive; booleans are invalid.
Define similarity as zero whenever either vector is zero. Handle large and tiny finite vectors safely.
Reject invalid shapes, non-finite values, or invalid k with ValueError. Leave all inputs unchanged.

hints.title: Normalize safely
hints.body: Scale each vector by its largest absolute coordinate before taking its length.

hints.title: Treat zeros explicitly
hints.body: A zero query gives all rows equal scores. A zero document gets score zero.

hints.title: Use a secondary key
hints.body: Sort by negative score first, then by row index. np.lexsort can express this deterministic ordering.

explanation: Cosine ranking depends on direction, not vector length. A longer embedding is not automatically a more relevant document.
Tie-breaking is part of the contract: deterministic results make evaluation and debugging reproducible.
This exact scan is a baseline for small corpora. Approximate indexes become useful at larger scales, where latency and recall trade off.
